items.rationale: The tiled panel (2.4×0.85 + 2.4×0.4 ≈ 3 m²) was in the damage area, so relaying it is covered repair cost. Priced at the upper customary tiling rate.
One hole was needed through a new tile for the pipe, so this is necessary repair work. Price taken from the prior (about 70 per hole).
Replacement tiles of the same cheap standard size; 3 m² matches the damaged area. Cheapest-range tile price.
About 1 m² of render around the bend had gone soft to the brick and was built back up before tiling.
Tiles are already charged in line 3. This oversized, non-standard format is a duplicate and an upgrade under 3.5(a) and 3.5(d).
Matches the documented joints: 2.4 m corner plus about 1.25 m up the panel end. Customary silicone joint rate.
Duplicates the silicone in line 6, uses a premium grade and a quantity inconsistent with the damage (3.5(a), (d), (e)).
First travel charge on the tiler's document, so reimbursable under 7.4.2. Price from the prior (about 80).
Labour for tiling is already in the unit rates (7.4.1). 14 h is excessive for a 3 m² panel and likely includes the uninsured attic work (3.5(e)). If paid at all, a reduced share.
Wiping down the reinstated tiles within the damage area stays part of repair cost (3.5(c)). It may, however, be treated as included in the tiling rate.
The wet plasterboard boxing was in the damage area. Its removal falls under demolition / opening up (5.1).

items.description: Removal and disposal of damaged insulation
items.rationale: The wet mineral wool was disposed of separately from the container load, so it is not a duplicate. Price from the prior (about 74).
Damp render behind the panel over about 3 m² was hacked off; this is necessary demolition in the damage area.
Old staining from the roof re-felting is unrelated to this leak and is upkeep in an undamaged element (3.5(b)).
The cover ring cracked when the tiles were removed, so it is consequential repair. A standard chrome ring is cheap.
Covers undoing and remaking the leaking joint with a new olive, which earlier cases indemnified as joint repair. Moderate flat charge.
Technical drying (5.2.7) supported by readings: normal after one week, machine collected the next morning. The owner's own dehumidifier is not billed.
Reimbursable only if attributable to materials actually used, such as the olive and sealing paste (7.4.4); otherwise it is an overhead.
About 1 m of sodden lagging was replaced like for like. Price from the prior (about 22 per m).
The drying firm's container took the tiles, render and board: debris removal reimbursed once (5.2.1). Price from the prior (about 60).
